dedupe_keys.name: san francisco existing buildings benchmark reports

description: Annual energy benchmarking results for buildings covered by San Francisco's Existing Buildings Energy Performance Ordinance, published by SF Environment on DataSF. Each row is one year of benchmarking for one building, so a building appears many times. The row shows compliance status and, if the building complied, energy use for gas, electricity and steam and EPA-estimated operational carbon emissions. The ordinance (Environment Code Chapter 20) requires each non-residential building with at least 10,000 square feet of conditioned space and each residential building with at least 50,000 square feet to benchmark yearly in Energy Star Portfolio Manager, and non-residential buildings to do an energy audit, retrocommissioning or a decarbonisation plan every five years. Fields include parcel number, address, floor area, category, property type, year built, benchmark year, ENERGY STAR score, site and source energy use intensity, weather-normalised intensities, greenhouse gas emissions, electricity, gas and steam use, latitude and longitude, and neighbourhood. Coverage: San Francisco. Access: open download and API on DataSF, refreshed monthly; the portal showed it last updated on 26 September 2026. Licence: Open Data Commons Public Domain Dedication and License; cost free. Caveats: figures are self-reported by owners, and exempt buildings have no energy values. Useful for city-scale energy and emissions planning; related records are not yet linked.
